outlook.statement: The outlook for small NBFCs in India for current fiscal year looks positive with expected growth in assets under management and an increasing role in supporting the socioeconomic construct of Indian economy with a focus on financial inclusion.

risks: Phased increase in minimum Net Owned Fund to ₹10 crore by March 2027
Shift to 90-day overdue NPA recognition norm pushing up reported NPAs and provisioning
Higher funding costs compared to banks with limited access to diverse capital sources
Rising technology and compliance expenses due to RBI reporting and automation mandates
Difficulties in attracting experienced Directors and skilled compliance professionals
Regulatory tightening extending more stringent capital and governance norms to base-layer entities
Competition from banks and larger NBFCs in small-ticket lending eroding margins
Credit risk in borrower segments vulnerable to income shocks (poor monsoons, inflation, economic slowdowns)
Sector-wide trust damage from isolated failures among small NBFCs
Increased fraud and cyber risk from digital channels without strong internal controls
Inherent limitations of internal financial controls including possibility of collusion or improper management override
Projections of internal financial controls evaluation to future periods subject to risk of controls becoming inadequate due to changes in conditions or deterioration in compliance
Market risk (price risk on equity/preference/debt instruments at FVTPL)
Credit risk (counterparty default, managed via credit quality review, counterparty limits, collateral revisions)
Liquidity risk (managed via cash flow forecasting, maturity profiling, debt covenants compliance)
Interest rate risk (no floating rate borrowings as at March 31, 2026 and 2025)
Foreign currency risk (no foreign currency exposure)
Contingent liabilities: Guarantees given for loans taken by others, limited to investment property mortgaged (book value Rs 210.20 lakh), litigation proceedings in progress
